title: Airgap KMS Bridge Orchestration Proposal v0.1 (draft)
content:
Purpose and scope

This draft proposes an orchestration pattern and migration playbook for customers running Redwood Private in air-gapped or highly restricted VPCs who want: (a) BYOK/BYOK-HSM with offline key custody, (b) auditable, immutable event forwarding for key-operations, and (c) terraform-driven lifecycle for upgrade and rollback. The goal is to enable secure HSM-backed key usage without requiring persistent egress from the customer site, while preserving centralized audit and SRE observability via store-and-forward bridges.

High-level design summary

- KMS Bridge: a lightweight on-site agent (go binary) that performs signed, rate-limited, store-and-forward operations between on-prem HSM/KMS and Redwood control plane over approved channels (e.g., customer-bidirectional bastion or scheduled export packages).
- Offline Key Attestation: use challenge-response attestation using signed blobs exported from HSM for model-enclave bootstrap. No private key material leaves the HSM in plaintext.
- Audit Forwarding: local append-only audit ledger (WAL) stored on immutable storage (WORM or write-once object) and periodically packaged and pushed via an operator-controlled channel to a designated audit sink (S3-compatible endpoint) with integrity proofs (SHA-256 + signed manifest).
- Terraform modules: provide idempotent resources for bridge configuration, agent installation, manifest signing policies, and vault-secrets-binding. Modules will be parameterized to support both PKCS#11 HSMs and cloud-KMS connectors.

Operational flow (day-to-day)

1. Key generation: operator generates keys on the customer HSM or imports keys using a secure key ceremony. A signed attestation blob is created and stored locally.
2. Provisioning: Terraform deploys KMS bridge config, agent systemd unit, and local policy that restricts the bridge to only allowed commands (encrypt/decrypt/sign).
3. Request path: Redwood inference node requests cryptographic operations via local sidecar calling the KMS agent over a unix socket. Agent enforces rate limits and records an audit entry.
4. Audit sync: Agent appends ledger entries and on a scheduled window (configurable daily/weekly) packages encrypted manifest and pushes to the audit sink using operator-controlled transfer (airgap-support channel).

Security hardening controls (recommended)

- Minimum privileges: agent runs as a dedicated uid/gid, limited caps, locked-down seccomp profile.
- Immutable audit ledger: write-once files, periodic integrity checksum with remote signing key stored in separate HSM partition.
- Key usage policies: limit operations per key (ttl, max-requests/day), emergency freeze endpoint requiring multi-actor approval.
- Dual control for key export: require 2-of-3 operator approval for any key material movement.
- Fallback behavior: local-only decryption allowed during network outages; flagged as offline-mode in audit manifest and requires subsequent reconciliation.

Terraform notes and module sketch

- Module name: redwood_private_airgap_kms_bridge
- Resources to expose: bridge_config, agent_systemd_unit, local_ledger_bucket (optional), key_binding (vault secret), attestation_manifest_resource
- Variables: hsm_type (pkcs11|cloudkms), attestation_mode (onsite|ceremony), audit_push_schedule (cron), allowed_commands (list)
- Outputs: agent_unit_file, manifest_path, attestation_hash
- Upgrade strategy: create new module version and deploy alongside existing agent with feature-flagged behavior (dual-write mode). After 48-hour shadow period and audit verification, flip traffic via terraform apply to point sidecars to new agent socket.

Upgrade and rollback plan (stepwise)

Phase 0 - Preparation (T-30d to T-7d)
- Run full inventory of HSM firmware versions and PKCS#11 drivers.
- Confirm operator(s) for key-ceremony and emergency rollback.
- Create test-dev airgapped environment with representative workload.

Phase 1 - Staged rollout (T-7d to T+3d)
- Deploy bridge v1.0 (readonly) in shadow mode; agent only logs calls but does not apply changes.
- Verify audit ledger format, signatures, and transfer mechanisms.
- Smoke tests: encrypt/decrypt loops, attestation validation.

Phase 2 - Dual-write and canary (T+4d to T+10d)
- Enable dual-write (old agent + new agent) and route 5% requests to new agent if applicable.
- Continuous verification of latency, error rates, and ledger diffs.

Phase 3 - Cutover (T+11d)
- Flip traffic to new agent after no discrepancies for 72 hours.
- Monitor audit manifests for missing entries and reconcile immediately.

Rollback
- Revert terraform to previous module version, re-enable old agent, and mark all keys used during failed window for manual audit.
- Preserve audit ledger snapshots and tag manifests with rollback-reason.

Testing checklist

- Unit: pkcs11 mock driver tests for all code paths.
- Integration: agent <-> HSM interaction tests using hardware emulator.
- Chaos: simulate network partition and validate store-and-forward recovery.
- Compliance: generate sample audit packages and validate signature chain against compliance checklist.

Open questions / TODOs

- Decide whether to support direct HSM-backed TLS for agent transport or wrap in mTLS using customer-provided certs.
- Finalize manifest schema versioning and include schema migration story.
- Add support for encrypted incremental diffs to reduce package sizes over low-bandwidth links.
- Define retention and tamper-evidence window for local ledger (60 days vs 365 days).

Stakeholders

- Security: Maya Chen (policy + compliance)
- Infra: Rohit Patel (agent + terraform)
- SRE: Ethan Brooks (observability + audit sink)
- Solutions Eng: TBD for customer rollout support

Appendix: quick commands and debug tips

- Validate agent is running: sudo systemctl status redwood-kms-bridge
- View local ledger head: tail -n 100 /var/lib/redwood-kms/ledger.log
- Package manifest locally: /opt/redwood/bin/bridge-package --out /tmp/manifest.tar.gz --sign-key /etc/bridge/signing.pem
- Replayer for audit: /opt/redwood/bin/audit-replay --manifest /tmp/manifest.tar.gz --target-sink s3://redwood-audit-test

Notes to reviewers

This is intentionally high-level and operational. I want feedback on the store-and-forward model, the expected bandwidth assumptions for customers (low-bandwidth vs fully air-gapped), and the terraform upgrade workflow. Please comment inline or ping #private-deployments on Slack.

References

- CONFLUENCE-PLAT-8452: Airgap KMS patterns (internal)
- JIRA-PD-1293: Bridge agent initial implementation
- github.com/redwood-inference/terraform-modules/pull/412 (prototype module)
